---
title: "Figure 3 — the calibration cascade: from the residual to the accumulated score information"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
CURATED single-figure alternative that merges the essential rows of Figure 3 (residual, data
level) and Figure 4 (score, inference level) into one calibration CASCADE, reading the same 5
ensemble CSVs figures/data/figure_3_time_dlik_{NR,R,NMR,MR,IR}.csv (each ~1 GB, 1000 sims; cell
N_ch=100, Current_Noise=1e-4, interval=0.1 tau) ONCE each. Time axis in milliseconds.

ONE OUTPUT: Figure_3.pdf, 7.0 x 7.5 in. Settled 2026-07-30 after comparing four candidates (six
rows against seven, one parameter against two); the three that lost were deleted rather than left
behind as dead code, so what remains builds the chosen figure and nothing else.

ROSTER: four columns, the cost ladder LSE -> NR -> R -> IR (this paragraph used to say five
columns NR/MNR/R/MR/IR, which predates the merged roster).

PARAMETERS: two, k_off and N_ch, one colour each, on the score rows; rows A and B are
parameter-free and neutral grey. The calibration is close to parameter-independent, which is why
one representative parameter used to be enough, but the INFORMATION is not, which is what the F_t
row is about. N_ch is not drawn in the least-squares column (see the note at SC).

Rows A-F are TIME (agonist shading), row G is LAG at the very bottom. The Fisher row sits between
the data rows and the inference rows because it is a PRECONDITION, not a step in the cascade: there
is no point asking whether the reported information is honest before establishing that there is
information, and for how long.
  A predicted & observed current   (one example recording: the data + the filter's prediction band;
    the ENSEMBLE-MEAN total logL over recordings +/- SE annotated per column: recursive ~ -145,
    naive ~ -230, an ~87-nat gap: the data is ~e^87 more probable under the recursive/conditional filters)
  B residual variance  mean_t[r_t^2] ~ 1   (data 2nd moment; r_t=(patch-y_mean)/sqrt(y_var))
  C per-step Fisher information  F_t   (where in the recording each parameter is measured at all;
    the N_ch information dies when the agonist is washed out, the k_off information does not)
  D score bias, standardized  sbar_t/sqrt(Fbar_t) ~ 0   (inference 1st moment; dimensionless, so
    two parameters with different units can share one axis)
  E per-interval information ratio  Var_recordings(s_t)/mean_recordings(F_t) ~ 1
    (inference 2nd moment, LOCAL: the sampling-distortion information; F_t = dmu^2/v + 0.5 dv^2/v^2)
  F accumulated information ratio  Var(sum s_t)/sum F_t = J_T/F_T ~ 1
    (inference 2nd moment, GLOBAL: the score correlation accumulates -> the overconfidence of
     Figure 2; the naive pair diverges, the recursive trio stays near 1)
  G score autocorrelation (lag) ~ 0   (the temporal memory that MAKES F diverge)

The story: the prediction is miscalibrated in variance (B); there is information at all only over
part of the recording, and for how long depends on the parameter (C); the score is biased (D); the
information identity holds per interval (E ~ 1) but the accumulated identity fails (F diverges)
exactly BECAUSE the score carries temporal memory (G).

SYSTEMATIC CONVENTION: any non-negative quantity (a variance or a ratio of variances) is on a
log10 y-axis with the reference value (1) always on the ticks; signed quantities (current, bias,
ACF) are linear with 0 forced onto the ticks. The Fisher row is the exception: log10(F_t) on a
linear axis, because it never passes near 1 and forcing 1 onto its ticks would be meaningless.
Rows B, E and F use a separate scale per block (naive LSE/NR | recursive R/IR); E is shared (~1).
BANDS: every band in the figure is a nonparametric bootstrap over the 1000 recordings, B = 400
replicates, percentile interval. One convention throughout, so that comparing band widths across
rows compares one kind of object. The single exception is row A, whose band is not an uncertainty
at all but the filter's own predictive +-1 sd for the one example recording.

RENDER: reads 5 GB, too heavy for a laptop; run where figures/data/ resolves.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r read}
# Merged-paper roster: the cost ladder LSE -> NR -> R -> IR (the recursive-mechanism ladder R/MR/VR/IR
# is a supplement). All algorithms stay in the DUMP; only the panel roster changes here. LSE and NR are
# the non-recursive (open-loop) pair, so they share the "naive" y-scale block below. Set ALGOS back to
# c("R","MR","VR","IR") for the recursive-ladder figure.
ALGOS  <- c("LSE", "NR", "R", "IR")
ALAB   <- c(LSE = "LSE", NR = "NR", NMR = "MNR", R = "R", MR = "MR", VR = "VR", IR = "IR")
LEAD   <- ALGOS[1]      # leftmost column: carries the y title, the row titles and the panel tags
FULL   <- c(LSE = "Least Squares", NR = "Non-Recursive", NMR = "Mean Non-Recursive", R = "Recursive",
            VR = "Variance Recursive", MR = "Mean Recursive", IR = "Interval Recursive")
P_MAIN <- 1L     # k_off
B      <- 400    # bootstrap replicates over recordings

read_one <- function(a) {
  dt  <- fread(sprintf("../data/figure_3_time_dlik_%s.csv", a), skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  agg <- function(d) d[, .(v = mean(value)), by = .(simulation_index, sample_index)]  # dedup writer x2 copies
  pk  <- function(comp, calc, p = NA) {
    q <- dt[component_path == comp & calculus == calc & !is.na(sample_index)]
    if (!is.na(p)) q <- q[param_index == p]
    agg(q)
  }
  rr <- pk("r_std",  "primitive");          setnames(rr, "v", "r_std")
  ll <- pk("logL",   "primitive");          setnames(ll, "v", "ll")   # the OUTPUT: per-interval logL
  yv <- pk("y_var",  "primitive");          setnames(yv, "v", "yv")
  ti <- unique(dt[!is.na(patch_current), .(sample_index, t = step_middle * 1000, agonist)])  # ms
  ti <- ti[, .(t = first(t), agonist = first(agonist)), by = sample_index]
  # example recording (min sim): predicted current mean/var (primitives) over the observed current
  es  <- dt[!is.na(sample_index), min(simulation_index)]
  eb  <- unique(dt[simulation_index == es & !is.na(patch_current),
                   .(sample_index, t = step_middle * 1000, obs = patch_current, agonist)])
  eb  <- eb[, .(t = first(t), obs = first(obs), agonist = first(agonist)), by = sample_index]
  em  <- dt[simulation_index == es & component_path == "y_mean" & calculus == "primitive" & !is.na(sample_index),
            .(y_mean = mean(value)), by = sample_index]
  ev  <- dt[simulation_index == es & component_path == "y_var"  & calculus == "primitive" & !is.na(sample_index),
            .(y_var  = mean(value)), by = sample_index]
  ex  <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "sample_index"), list(eb, em, ev))
  # The per-interval score s_t and its per-step Gaussian Fisher information I = F_t, for each
  # parameter in PSC. Every row of the figure that is about a parameter descends from this one
  # table, including the Fisher row, which is just E[I] and so needs no separate extraction.
  # `sco` is long, one block per parameter, so the downstream statistics group by (algo, param).
  # Extracted while dt is still in memory: the second parameter costs no extra pass over the
  # ~1 GB dump. param_index in the dump: 0 = k_on, 1 = k_off, 2 = unitary_current, 5 = Num_ch_mean.
  PSC <- c(k_off = P_MAIN, N_ch = 5L)
  sco <- rbindlist(lapply(names(PSC), function(nm) {
    scp <- pk("logL",   "derivative", PSC[[nm]]); setnames(scp, "v", "s")
    dmp <- pk("y_mean", "derivative", PSC[[nm]]); setnames(dmp, "v", "dm")
    dvp <- pk("y_var",  "derivative", PSC[[nm]]); setnames(dvp, "v", "dv")
    z <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("simulation_index", "sample_index")),
                list(scp, dmp, dvp, yv))
    z[, .(algo = a, param = nm, simulation_index, sample_index, s,
          I = dm^2 / yv + 0.5 * dv^2 / yv^2)]
  }))
  rm(dt); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  rr <- merge(rr, ll, by = c("simulation_index", "sample_index"))
  rr <- merge(rr, ti, by = "sample_index")
  list(resid = rr[is.finite(r_std)][, algo := a],
       sco   = sco,
       ex    = ex[, algo := a],
       tm    = ti)
}
raw  <- lapply(ALGOS, read_one)
RR   <- rbindlist(lapply(raw, `[[`, "resid")); RR[, algo := factor(algo, levels = ALGOS)]
SC   <- rbindlist(lapply(raw, `[[`, "sco"));   SC[, algo := factor(algo, levels = ALGOS)]
# SC carries both parameters. SCk is the k_off slice, kept because the lag axis and the caption
# numbers are k_off statements; PSEL_COL fixes which parameters the figure shows.
PSEL_COL <- c("k_off", "N_ch")
SC[, param := factor(param, levels = PSEL_COL)]
# N_ch is NOT shown in the least-squares column. Its diagonal information there is not zero, but it
# comes from the mean current N*i*P_open, along which the channel count and the unitary current are
# degenerate; separating them needs the gating fluctuations, which is the one thing least squares
# does not model. The curve would therefore read as information about N_ch that least squares does
# not deliver. figure_4_common.R applies the same exclusion through EXCLUDE_ROWS, so this keeps
# figure 3 consistent with figure 4 rather than inventing a rule. One filter here covers the score
# rows, the ratio rows and the autocorrelation, since all of them descend from SC; SCk is k_off
# only, so the mono figures are untouched.
SC <- SC[!(param == "N_ch" & algo == "LSE")]
SCk  <- SC[param == "k_off"]
EX   <- rbindlist(lapply(raw, `[[`, "ex"));    EX[, algo := factor(algo, levels = ALGOS)]
tmap <- raw[[1]]$tm
setorder(RR, algo, simulation_index, sample_index)
setorder(SC, algo, simulation_index, sample_index)
n_samp <- uniqueN(RR$sample_index)
```

```{r residual-stats}
# Panel A annotation: the ensemble-mean total logL over recordings +/- its SE. Per-recording total
# logL first (sum_t logL_t within a recording), then mean and SE across the 1000 recordings.
totL <- RR[, .(tot = sum(ll)), by = .(algo, simulation_index)][
              , .(mean = mean(tot), se = sd(tot) / sqrt(.N)), by = algo]
# Row B: residual variance over time. Bootstrap over recordings, like every other band in this
# figure. For a mean over 1000 recordings the percentile interval and 1.96*SE agree to within a
# couple of percent, so this buys consistency rather than accuracy: a reader comparing band widths
# across rows should be comparing one kind of object, not two.
bootmean <- function(d, val) {
  M <- as.matrix(dcast(d, simulation_index ~ sample_index, value.var = val)[, -1])
  n <- nrow(M)
  rep <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) colMeans(M[sample.int(n, n, TRUE), , drop = FALSE]),
                numeric(ncol(M)))
  data.table(sample_index = as.integer(colnames(M)), m = colMeans(M),
             lo = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
             hi = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
RR[, r2 := r_std^2]
tsV <- RR[, bootmean(.SD, "r2"), by = algo]
setnames(tsV, c("m", "lo", "hi"), c("mean_r2", "r2_lo", "r2_hi"))
tsV <- merge(tsV, tmap, by = "sample_index")[, algo := factor(algo, levels = ALGOS)]
# Row F: SCORE autocorrelation over lag (the k_off score s_t; mean over recordings +/- 1.96 SE per
# lag). Same computation as figure_3's row E, so this panel matches it. This is the temporal memory
# at the inference level: a non-white score IS the J_T > F_T that makes the accumulated ratio (E)
# diverge. (Residual autocorrelation, the data-level version, stays in the full figure_3.)
LAGMAX  <- min(25, n_samp - 2)
acf_one <- function(x) as.numeric(acf(x, lag.max = LAGMAX, plot = FALSE)$acf)
# Bootstrap here too, and it is nearly free: the per-recording autocorrelations are already
# computed and stacked in M, so a replicate is a row resample of M followed by colMeans. No
# autocorrelation is ever recomputed.
acf_by <- function(D) as_tibble(D) %>%
  group_by(algo, param, simulation_index) %>% summarise(a = list(acf_one(s)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(algo, param) %>% summarise(M = list(do.call(rbind, a)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(d = map(M, function(m) {
    n <- nrow(m)
    rep <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) colMeans(m[sample.int(n, n, TRUE), , drop = FALSE]),
                  numeric(ncol(m)))
    tibble(lag = 0:LAGMAX, acf = colMeans(m),
           lo = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
           hi = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
  })) %>%
  select(algo, param, d) %>% unnest(d) %>% filter(lag >= 1)
acf_sc  <- acf_by(SCk)    # k_off only: feeds the lag axis and the caption numbers, not a panel
acf_sc2 <- acf_by(SC)     # both parameters: the *_color variants
```

```{r score-stats}
set.seed(1)
colVar    <- function(M) { n <- nrow(M); m <- colMeans(M); (colMeans(M * M) - m^2) * n / (n - 1) }
rowCumsum <- function(M) t(apply(M, 1, cumsum))
# All four per-interval statistics come out of ONE resampling loop, so the three added here cost a
# couple of colMeans per replicate; the expensive part, the rowCumsum for the accumulated ratio,
# was already there.
# The standardized score bias is resampled as the WHOLE ratio, colMeans(Sb)/sqrt(colMeans(Ib)),
# not as the numerator with the denominator held fixed. That is a real correction and not just
# consistency: s_t and I_t are computed from the same recordings and are correlated, and the
# analytic standard error this replaces ignored that correlation by treating Fbar as known.
compute_one <- function(d) {
  Sm  <- as.matrix(dcast(d, simulation_index ~ sample_index, value.var = "s")[, -1])
  Im  <- as.matrix(dcast(d, simulation_index ~ sample_index, value.var = "I")[, -1])
  smp <- as.integer(colnames(Sm)); n <- nrow(Sm)
  vA  <- colVar(Sm); Fb <- colMeans(Im)
  zA  <- colMeans(Sm) / sqrt(Fb)
  rB  <- vA / Fb
  rC  <- colVar(rowCumsum(Sm)) / cumsum(Fb)
  repZ <- repF <- repB <- repC <- matrix(NA_real_, B, length(smp))
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    Sb  <- Sm[idx, , drop = FALSE]; Ib <- Im[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    fb  <- colMeans(Ib)
    repZ[b, ] <- colMeans(Sb) / sqrt(fb)
    repF[b, ] <- fb
    repB[b, ] <- colVar(Sb) / fb
    repC[b, ] <- colVar(rowCumsum(Sb)) / cumsum(fb)
  }
  ci <- function(M, p) apply(M, 2, quantile, p, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.table(sample_index = smp, mA = colMeans(Sm), Fbar = Fb,
             zA = zA,   zA_lo = ci(repZ, .025), zA_hi = ci(repZ, .975),
             F_lo = ci(repF, .025), F_hi = ci(repF, .975),
             rB = rB,   rB_lo = ci(repB, .025), rB_hi = ci(repB, .975),
             rC = rC,   rC_lo = ci(repC, .025), rC_hi = ci(repC, .975))
}

# Same statistics per (algo, param) for the *_color variants. This is the expensive part of the
# notebook: compute_one runs B = 400 bootstrap replicates over the 1000 recordings, so a second
# parameter doubles it. Everything else in this refactor is free.
RES2 <- SC[, compute_one(.SD), by = .(algo, param)]
RES2 <- merge(RES2, tmap, by = "sample_index")
RES2[, `:=`(algo = factor(algo, levels = ALGOS), param = factor(param, levels = PSEL_COL))]
# ONE mask for both score rows, and it is an absolute floor rather than a fraction of the peak.
# The score bias and the information ratio are the same 0/0 as F_t goes to zero -- both are built
# from the same two derivatives -- so masking one and not the other is an inconsistency, not a
# property of the quantities. What forces a mask is numerical, not statistical: once the
# derivatives reach ~1e-15 the ratio is floating-point noise. A percent-of-peak threshold (this
# used to be Fbar > 1e-3 * max(Fbar)) erases the low-information region by construction, which is
# precisely the region the N_ch curve is about.
FMIN <- 1e-6
dF2 <- RES2[is.finite(Fbar) & Fbar > FMIN]                       # row C: the information itself
dScore2 <- RES2[is.finite(zA) & is.finite(Fbar) & Fbar > FMIN]   # row D
dB2 <- RES2[is.finite(rB) & is.finite(rB_lo) & rB_lo > 0 & is.finite(Fbar) & Fbar > FMIN]
dC2 <- RES2[is.finite(rC) & is.finite(rC_lo) & rC_lo > 0]
```

```{r panels, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 6.2}
COL <- "#0072B2"; NUL <- "#009E73"
# the two-block y scale only exists while a non-recursive column is present; with an all-recursive
# roster `naive` is empty, every column falls in one group and the split degenerates to one scale.
naive <- intersect(ALGOS, c("LSE", "NR", "NMR")); recg <- setdiff(ALGOS, naive)

grange <- function(lo, hi, algo, pad = .08) {
  g <- tibble(lo, hi, grp = ifelse(algo %in% naive, 1L, 2L)) %>% group_by(grp) %>%
    summarise(lo = min(lo), hi = max(hi), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pd = (hi - lo) * pad, lo = lo - pd, hi = hi + pd)
  list(naive = c(g$lo[g$grp == 1], g$hi[g$grp == 1]), rec = c(g$lo[g$grp == 2], g$hi[g$grp == 2]))
}
padr <- function(r, f = .06) r + c(-1, 1) * diff(r) * f
ratio_breaks <- function(lo, hi) {
  cand <- if (log10(hi) - log10(lo) <= 1.2)
            c(.1, .2, .3, .5, .7, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, 70, 100)
          else c(.1, .2, .5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)
  b <- sort(unique(c(1, cand[cand >= lo & cand <= hi])))
  # At most three labels. The rows are short (see the height budget at the layout chunk), so a
  # full ladder of breaks would collide; 1 is the reference and must survive, the other two are
  # the ends of the range actually drawn.
  if (length(b) > 3) b <- sort(unique(c(b[1], 1, b[length(b)])))
  b
}
# The gap under the column heads has three sources, all of them furniture. theme_void inherits
# plot.margin from theme_grey (5.5 pt top and bottom), the title carries a default bottom margin
# of about half a line, and, worst of the three, the empty panel of this plot is a null unit that
# absorbs every bit of slack left in the header cell -- and that slack sits exactly between the
# titles and row A. The margins are zeroed here; the slack is removed by giving the header row a
# share slightly smaller than the two lines of text need (see HS2 at the layout chunk), so the
# panel collapses to zero height and the titles end flush against the first row.
colhead <- function(k) ggplot() + theme_void() + ggtitle(ALAB[[k]], subtitle = FULL[[k]]) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5, size = 9, margin = margin(b = 0.5)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = .5, size = 7, margin = margin(b = 0)),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
deco <- function(p, col, split, xr, yl, yq, ttl = NULL, tag = NULL, bottom = FALSE, xlab = NULL, logr = FALSE) {
  ylim <- if (is.list(yl)) (if (col %in% naive) yl$naive else yl$rec) else yl
  if (logr) {
    ylim <- c(min(ylim[1], 1), max(ylim[2], 1))
    rb <- ratio_breaks(ylim[1], ylim[2])
    p <- p + scale_y_log10(breaks = rb, labels = as.character(rb)) + coord_cartesian(xlim = xr, ylim = ylim)
  } else {
    brk <- pretty(ylim, n = 3); brk <- sort(unique(c(0, brk))); brk <- brk[brk >= ylim[1] & brk <= ylim[2]]
    if (length(brk) > 3) brk <- sort(unique(c(brk[1], 0, brk[length(brk)])))   # same cap; 0 is the reference
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = brk) + coord_cartesian(xlim = xr, ylim = ylim)
  }
  if (col == LEAD) p <- p + ylab(yq) + theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8))
  else if (col == "R" && split) p <- p + theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
  else p <- p + theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  # x NUMBERS on every bottom-of-block panel, but the x TITLE only ONCE, on the centre column (R)
  if (bottom) {
    if (col == "R") p <- p + xlab(xlab) + theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8))
    else p <- p + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
  } else p <- p + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
  # Neither the row title nor the A-F letter is drawn here any more; see the house convention in
  # papers/_program/notation_map.md section 6. R3: the prose name of a row lives in the legend,
  # once, not inside the image. R4: the letter sits alone in its own strip column, added at the
  # layout chunk, which costs width once instead of a line of height per row (~0.13 in x 6).
  # `ttl` and `tag` are still accepted so the six call sites below need no edit.
  p + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0.5, 3, 0.5, 3))
}
base <- function() theme_bw(base_size = 8)

tr    <- range(tsV$t)
lr    <- range(c(1, acf_sc$lag))
agon  <- tmap[agonist > 0]; x0 <- min(agon$t); x1 <- max(agon$t)
# full-panel agonist band. ymin branches: a log10 axis rejects a negative floor
# (log10(<=0)=NaN -> rect dropped); linear panels go negative and need to reach the floor.
mkshade <- function(logr = FALSE) annotate("rect", xmin = x0, xmax = x1,
                  ymin = if (logr) 1e-10 else -1e10, ymax = 1e10, fill = "grey85", alpha = .5)

# A: example recording — predicted current (mean +/- sd) over observed; SHARED, linear, time. Extra
# top headroom (+35% of the range) carries the ensemble-mean total logL over recordings (+/- SE) as a
# per-column label. Spelled "mean logL" (over recordings) so it is not misread as this one example's
# logL; on two lines so it fits the narrow single-column width without clipping.
yTr <- padr(range(c(EX$obs, EX$y_mean - sqrt(EX$y_var), EX$y_mean + sqrt(EX$y_var)), na.rm = TRUE))
yTr[2] <- yTr[2] + 0.35 * diff(yTr)
# B: residual variance (>=0) -> log10, GROUPED, time
loV <- pmax(tsV$r2_lo, 1e-6)
yA  <- lapply(grange(log10(loV), log10(tsV$r2_hi), as.character(tsV$algo)), function(r) 10^r)
# --- numbers the caption quotes, printed so they are never read off the plot (LINT-SRC) ---
.capnum <- merge(
  totL[, .(algo, logL = mean, logL_se = se)],
  RES2[param == "k_off"][, .SD[which.max(sample_index)], by = algo][
        , .(algo, accum_ratio = rC, lo = rC_lo, hi = rC_hi)],
  by = "algo")
.capnum <- merge(.capnum, as.data.table(acf_sc)[lag == 1, .(algo, acf_lag1 = acf,
                 acf_lo = lo, acf_hi = hi)], by = "algo")
.capnum <- .capnum[match(ALGOS, algo)]
cat("\n=== Figure 3 caption numbers (n_simulations =", uniqueN(SC$simulation_index), ") ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(.capnum), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
cat("logL spread (best - worst):", sprintf("%.1f nats\n", diff(range(.capnum$logL))))

# HEIGHT BUDGET (2026-07-30). The eLife text block is 9.23 in tall and this figure's legend runs
# about 2.9 in at 9 pt, so the image has to fit in ~6.3 in. All six rows are kept; what changes is
# that the rows no longer get equal shares. A, the example trace, needs vertical range because it
# IS a range; B, C and D are curves sitting on a reference line, where extra height buys nothing;
# E spans 1 to 15 on a log axis and F spans 0 to 0.86, so both need something in between. The head
# strip is raised from 0.10 to 0.18 because at 6.2 in the old share (0.16 in) is less than the
# column titles themselves need (~0.27 in) and they would clip.
# The total stays at 6.2 in after folding the A-F letters into the row titles (see deco): the ~1 in
# that change frees is spent on the panels rather than on shrinking the figure further, because at
# 6.2 in the data area was tighter than anything else in this family. 6.2 + a 2.9 in legend is 9.1
# against the 9.23 in text block, so the figure and its legend share one page.
# Head at 0.15, deliberately a little less than the two lines of text need. The fixed title rows
# keep their height and the empty panel under them collapses to zero, which is what removes the gap
# between the heads and row A. Raise it only if the subtitles start to clip. The vector in force is
# HS2, at the layout chunk; the six-row HS that used to sit here went with the six-row figure.

# Row furniture as two thin columns instead of a line of height per row. On the LEFT the panel
# letter alone, bold, at the top, which is where eLife figures put it. On the RIGHT the row title
# rotated in a grey box, which is where ggplot's own facet_grid puts a row strip.
#
# The box is drawn as a rect INSIDE the plotting area rather than as plot.background, because a
# plot background also paints the margin, so consecutive rows fuse into one continuous grey bar
# with no separation. ymin/ymax at 0.03/0.97 leave the gap between boxes that a facet strip has.
#
# Titles are wrapped to two lines and carry no math. A rotated title has to fit in the ROW's
# height, and the short rows are 0.84 in: "information ratio" at 6.5 pt is 0.72 in, the full
# "per-interval information ratio" on one line would be 1.46 in and would not fit. The symbols
# stay on the y axis (notation_map.md section 6, R3 and R5); the strip is a locator.
rowlet <- function(lt) ggplot() + theme_void() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.97, label = lt, size = 8 / .pt, fontface = "bold", vjust = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

rowstrip <- function(txt) ggplot() + theme_void() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.15, xmax = 1, ymin = 0.03, ymax = 0.97, fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.575, y = 0.5, label = txt, angle = -90, size = 6.5 / .pt,
           lineheight = 0.9) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

RTTL <- c(A = "predicted &\nobserved current", B = "residual\nvariance",
          C = "Fisher\ninformation",  D = "score bias",
          E = "per-interval\ninformation ratio", F = "accumulated\ninformation ratio",
          G = "score\nautocorrelation")

```

```{r color-variants, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 7.3}
# TWO-PARAMETER VARIANTS, written under their own names so all four can be compared:
#   Figure_3.pdf            6 rows, k_off only            (the current figure)
#   Figure_3_FIM.pdf        7 rows, k_off only + F_t row
#   Figure_3_color.pdf      6 rows, k_off and N_ch
#   Figure_3_FIM_color.pdf  7 rows, k_off and N_ch + F_t row
#
# Rows A and B are parameter-free (the current, and the standardized residual), so they are shared
# with the mono figures unchanged. Rows C to F are score quantities and get one colour per
# parameter. k_off keeps the mono figure's blue, so a colour variant can be laid over the mono one
# and the k_off curves should coincide exactly.
#
# WHAT THE LEGEND MUST SAY (Luciano, 2026-07-30). The least-squares column carries no N_ch curve,
# by exclusion rather than by absence of data (see the note at SC in the read chunk). Least squares
# does not model the gating fluctuations, which is the only thing that separates the channel count
# from the unitary current, so its information about N_ch would be an artefact of the
# parameterisation rather than something it delivers. A sentence of the form "the channel-count
# comparison is not drawn for least squares, because with the fluctuations unmodelled the channel
# count and the unitary current are not separable" belongs in the legend; without it the missing
# curve reads as a rendering failure.
PCOL2 <- c(k_off = COL, N_ch = "#D55E00")
PLEG2 <- parse(text = c('k["off"]', 'N["ch"]'))
# ONE legend for the whole figure, and it takes two things to get it.
# drop = FALSE: since N_ch is excluded from the least-squares column, that panel has a single level
# present, and by default ggplot drops unused levels from the guide. Its guide would then differ
# from the others, and patchwork's guides = "collect" only merges guides that are identical, so
# every distinct one gets printed. Keeping both levels in every panel's scale makes them identical.
# guides(fill = "none"): the ribbons carry a fill scale with the same labels as the colour scale,
# which otherwise prints as a second legend saying the same thing. The colour key is the one that
# means something; the fill just follows it.
pscale <- list(scale_colour_manual(values = PCOL2, labels = PLEG2, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
               scale_fill_manual(values = PCOL2, labels = PLEG2, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
               guides(fill = "none"),
               # the one key that survives is a line, so make it read as one rather than as the
               # hairline the 0.4 pt data lines would give
               guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 0.8))))
# Rows A and B are not about any parameter -- they are the current and the standardized residual --
# so they must not wear a parameter's colour. Neutral dark grey for the line, light grey for the
# band, which also keeps them apart from the observed points at grey45.
NEU_L <- "#1A1A1A"; NEU_F <- "#9E9E9E"

# ONE legend in the whole figure, carried by exactly one panel. patchwork's guides = "collect"
# merges guides only when they are IDENTICAL, and ours are not: the autocorrelation row draws its
# key with points and segments while the ribbon rows draw it with a line, and the least-squares
# column has one level fewer than the rest. Rather than chase those differences, every geom is
# built with show.legend = FALSE except the Fisher line in the column named here, so only one guide
# is ever produced and collecting it is trivial. IR is the bearer because it carries both
# parameters; the least-squares column does not.
LEGCOL <- "IR"

# A and B rebuilt in the neutral colour for these variants (the mono figures keep COL).
pTr2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  d <- EX[algo == a]
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(t)) + mkshade() +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = y_mean - sqrt(y_var), ymax = y_mean + sqrt(y_var)),
                fill = NEU_F, alpha = .55) +
    geom_point(aes(y = obs), colour = "grey45", size = .35, alpha = .5) +
    geom_line(aes(y = y_mean), colour = NEU_L, linewidth = .4) +
    annotate("text", x = tr[2], y = yTr[2], hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 2.7, lineheight = .9,
             label = sprintf("mean logL\n%.1f %s %.1f", totL[algo == a, mean], "±",
                             totL[algo == a, se])) + base()
  deco(g, a, FALSE, tr, yTr, "current")
})
pA2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  d <- tsV[algo == a]
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(t, mean_r2)) + mkshade(TRUE) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(r2_lo, 1e-6), ymax = r2_hi), fill = NEU_F, alpha = .55) +
    geom_line(colour = NEU_L, linewidth = .4) + base()
  deco(g, a, TRUE, tr, yA, expression(bar(r[t]^2)), logr = TRUE)
})

# C: score bias, STANDARDIZED by its own information, s_bar_t / sqrt(F_bar_t).
# Two reasons, and the first is not cosmetic. (i) The raw score has the units of the parameter it
# differentiates, so k_off and N_ch cannot share a linear axis at all; dividing by sqrt(F_t) makes
# both dimensionless, with null 0 and natural scale 1, and comparable across members too.
# (ii) The raw version reached about -20 in the LSE and NR columns, because grange takes the
# absolute min and max over the block, so one excursion at the concentration jump set the scale for
# every other point. qrange below is grange's robust twin: the same naive/recursive split, but the
# block limits come from percentiles rather than extremes. A curve may therefore leave the panel;
# that is the intended trade and the legend should say so.
qrange <- function(lo, hi, algo, p = c(.005, .995), pad = .08) {
  g <- tibble(lo, hi, grp = ifelse(algo %in% naive, 1L, 2L)) %>% group_by(grp) %>%
    summarise(lo = quantile(lo, p[1], na.rm = TRUE),
              hi = quantile(hi, p[2], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pd = (hi - lo) * pad, lo = lo - pd, hi = hi + pd)
  list(naive = c(g$lo[g$grp == 1], g$hi[g$grp == 1]),
       rec   = c(g$lo[g$grp == 2], g$hi[g$grp == 2]))
}
yC2 <- qrange(dScore2$zA_lo, dScore2$zA_hi, as.character(dScore2$algo))
# One band only: the ordinary standard error of a mean over the recordings, standardized like the
# line. No bootstrap in this row -- the bootstrap in this notebook serves the two information-ratio
# rows, per-interval and accumulated, and nothing else.
# The ribbon is a bootstrap percentile interval of the WHOLE standardized ratio, resampled over
# recordings, so it carries the correlation between the score and its own information. The analytic
# standard error it replaces divided the numerator's error by a Fbar treated as known, which
# understates it wherever that correlation is not negligible.
pC2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(dScore2[algo == a], aes(t, zA, colour = param, fill = param)) + mkshade() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = zA_lo, ymax = zA_hi), alpha = .22, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4, show.legend = FALSE) + base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, TRUE, tr, yC2, expression(bar(s)[t] / sqrt(F[t])))
})
# D: per-interval information ratio, log10, shared
yD2 <- 10^padr(log10(as.numeric(quantile(c(dB2$rB_lo, dB2$rB_hi), c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE))))
pD2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(dB2[algo == a], aes(t, rB, colour = param, fill = param)) + mkshade(TRUE) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = rB_lo, ymax = rB_hi), alpha = .22, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4, show.legend = FALSE) + base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, FALSE, tr, yD2, expression(Var(s[t]) / F[t]), logr = TRUE)
})
# E: accumulated information ratio, log10, grouped, bottom of the time block
yE2 <- lapply(grange(log10(dC2$rC_lo), log10(dC2$rC_hi), as.character(dC2$algo)), function(r) 10^r)
pE2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(dC2[algo == a], aes(t, rC, colour = param, fill = param)) + mkshade(TRUE) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = rC_lo, ymax = rC_hi), alpha = .22, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4, show.legend = FALSE) + base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, TRUE, tr, yE2, expression(Var(sum(s[t])) / sum(F[t])),
       bottom = TRUE, xlab = "time (ms)", logr = TRUE)
})
# F: score autocorrelation over lag, signed -> linear, grouped, bottom of the lag block
yF2 <- grange(acf_sc2$lo, acf_sc2$hi, as.character(acf_sc2$algo))
pSc2 <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(filter(acf_sc2, algo == a), aes(lag, acf, colour = param)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = .35, show.legend = FALSE,
                   position = position_dodge(width = .35)) +
    geom_point(size = .25, position = position_dodge(width = .35), show.legend = FALSE) +
    base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, TRUE, lr, yF2, "ACF", bottom = TRUE, xlab = "lag")
})
# ROW C: the Fisher information itself, with its own bootstrap band. It comes from RES2's Fbar,
# the same table every other parameter row descends from, so there is one definition of F_t in the
# notebook and one resampling of it.
# Plotted as log10(F_t) on a LINEAR axis rather than through deco's log branch, because that branch
# forces the value 1 onto the ticks -- right for a ratio whose null is 1, meaningless for an
# information magnitude that spans decades and never passes near 1.
dF2[, `:=`(lF = log10(Fbar), lF_lo = log10(pmax(F_lo, 1e-300)), lF_hi = log10(F_hi))]
yFI <- range(c(dF2$lF_lo, dF2$lF_hi), finite = TRUE)
pFI <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(dF2[algo == a], aes(t, lF, colour = param, fill = param)) + mkshade() +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lF_lo, ymax = lF_hi), alpha = .22, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4, show.legend = (a == LEGCOL)) + base() + pscale +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = tr, ylim = yFI) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty(yFI, n = 3)) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0.5, 3, 0.5, 3),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
  if (a == LEAD)
    g + ylab(expression(log[10] ~ F[t])) + theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8))
  else
    g + theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
              axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
})

leg <- theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
             legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5), legend.key.size = unit(0.28, "cm"),
             legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
lay <- function(rows, hs) wrap_plots(
  c(list(plot_spacer()), lapply(ALGOS, colhead), list(plot_spacer()),
    unlist(lapply(seq_along(rows), function(k)
      c(list(rowlet(names(rows)[k])), rows[[k]]$p, list(rowstrip(rows[[k]]$s)))), recursive = FALSE)),
  ncol = length(ALGOS) + 2, widths = c(0.085, rep(1, length(ALGOS)), 0.155), heights = hs) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & leg


# Row weights, revisited with the final content: rows D, E and F each carry TWO curves and TWO
# ribbons, where the vector this replaces was set when every row had one of each. A is the trace and
# needs vertical range because its range IS the data; B is a single grey curve on a reference line;
# C spans decades; G is points with intervals over lag.
#        head   A(trace) B(resid) C(F_t) D(bias) E(ratio) F(accum) G(acf)
HS2 <- c(0.15,  0.85,    0.55,    0.70,  0.60,   0.60,    0.70,    0.70)

# ROW ORDER (2026-07-31). The Fisher row sits between the data rows and the inference rows, not
# inside the cascade. It is a PRECONDITION, not a step: there is no point asking whether the
# reported information is honest before establishing that there is information to report, and for
# how long. So: the recording and the prediction (A), whether the predictive variance is right (B),
# where in the recording each parameter is measured at all (C), and then the inference cascade in
# moment order -- the score is biased (D), the identity holds per interval (E), it fails once
# accumulated (F), and the reason is the temporal memory of the score (G).
g3d <- lay(list(A = list(p = pTr2, s = RTTL[["A"]]),
                B = list(p = pA2,  s = RTTL[["B"]]),
                C = list(p = pFI,  s = RTTL[["C"]]),
                D = list(p = pC2,  s = RTTL[["D"]]),
                E = list(p = pD2,  s = RTTL[["E"]]),
                F = list(p = pE2,  s = RTTL[["F"]]),
                G = list(p = pSc2, s = RTTL[["G"]])), HS2)
ggsave("Figure_3.pdf", g3d, width = 7.0, height = 7.5)
cat("wrote Figure_3.pdf: 7 rows, four columns, k_off and N_ch, 7.0 x 7.5 in\n")
```
